explanation:
[EFFECT] Temperature has a non-monotonic (inverted U-shaped) effect on predicted bike demand. Very cold temperatures (near 0°C) strongly suppress demand, with contributions as low as −0.8 in log space. Demand rises sharply as temperatures warm, peaking around 25–31°C (normalised temp ≈ 0.6–0.75), where the contribution is about +0.2, meaning noticeably more rentals are predicted. Above that sweet spot, demand starts to ease off again as temperatures become uncomfortably hot.

[IMPORTANCE] Temperature is the 3rd most important feature out of 9, with an importance score of 0.197. It has a substantial influence on predicted demand — particularly in its ability to drastically cut rentals during cold weather.

[RECOMMENDATION] Plan for significantly lower bike availability and staffing needs during cold periods (winter months with near-freezing temperatures), and ensure full fleet deployment and maintenance readiness during mild, warm weather around 25–30°C when demand is at its highest.
